passages.text: “Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture!” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD declares a warning.
The LORD addresses the shepherds.
The shepherds destroy the sheep of the LORD’s pasture.
The shepherds scatter the sheep of the LORD’s pasture.
The LORD says, “Woe to these shepherds.”
passages.original: ה֣וֹי רֹעִ֗ים מְאַבְּדִ֧ים וּמְפִצִ֛ים אֶת־ צֹ֥אן מַרְעִיתִ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the shepherds who tend My people: “You have scattered My flock and driven them away, and have not attended to them. Behold, I will attend to you for the evil of your deeds, declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks about the shepherds who care for His people.
The shepherds have scattered God's flock.
The shepherds have driven God's flock away.
The shepherds have not cared for God's flock.
The LORD will punish the shepherds for their evil deeds.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: לָ֠כֵן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַֽל־ הָרֹעִים֮ הָרֹעִ֣ים אֶת־ עַמִּי֒ אַתֶּ֞ם הֲפִצֹתֶ֤ם אֶת־ צֹאנִי֙ וַתַּדִּח֔וּם וְלֹ֥א פְקַדְתֶּ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם הִנְנִ֨י פֹקֵ֧ד עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם אֶת־ רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then I Myself will gather the remnant of My flock from all the lands to which I have banished them, and I will return them to their pasture, where they will be fruitful and multiply.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks about His people as His flock.
The LORD says He will act Himself.
The LORD will gather the remnant of His flock.
The remnant means those who remain after trouble.
The LORD will gather them from all the lands.
The LORD had banished them to these lands.
The LORD will bring them back.
The LORD will return them to their pasture.
The flock will live in their own land again.
The flock will be fruitful there.
The flock will multiply there.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֗י אֲקַבֵּץ֙ אֶת־ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית צֹאנִ֔י מִכֹּל֙ הָאֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ הִדַּ֥חְתִּי אֹתָ֖ם שָׁ֑ם וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֥י אֶתְהֶ֛ן עַל־ נְוֵהֶ֖ן וּפָר֥וּ וְרָבֽוּ׃

passages.text: I will raise up shepherds over them who will tend them, and they will no longer be afraid or dismayed, nor will any go missing, declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks about His people.
The LORD promises to act.
The LORD will raise up new shepherds over His people.
These shepherds will care for the people.
The people will not be afraid.
The people will not be dismayed.
No one will go missing.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֧י עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם רֹעִ֖ים וְרָע֑וּם וְלֹא־ יִֽירְא֨וּ ע֧וֹד וְלֹא־ יֵחַ֛תּוּ וְלֹ֥א יִפָּקֵ֖דוּ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and He will reign wisely as King and will administer justice and righteousness in the land.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises a future time.
The LORD says, “Days are coming.”
The LORD will act for David.
The LORD will raise up a Branch for David.
This Branch will be righteous.
This Branch will become King.
This King will rule with wisdom.
This King will do what is just.
This King will do what is right in the land.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וַהֲקִמֹתִ֥י לְדָוִ֖ד צֶ֣מַח צַדִּ֑יק וּמָ֤לַךְ מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ וְהִשְׂכִּ֔יל וְעָשָׂ֛ה מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: In His days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely. And this is His name by which He will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.
passages.sermon:
God will send a righteous King from David’s line.
This King will rule with wisdom.
He will do what is just and right.
During His reign, Judah will be saved.
Israel will live in safety.
People will call this King by a special name.
They will call Him “The LORD Our Righteousness.”
passages.original: בְּיָמָיו֙ תִּוָּשַׁ֣ע יְהוּדָ֔ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִשְׁכֹּ֣ן לָבֶ֑טַח וְזֶה־ שְּׁמ֥וֹ אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־ יִקְרְא֖וֹ יְהוָ֥ה׀ צִדְקֵֽנוּ׃ס

passages.text: So behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when they will no longer say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of the land of Egypt.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
He says, “The days are coming.
People will not say this anymore.
They will not say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites out of Egypt.’”
passages.original: לָכֵ֛ן הִנֵּֽה־ יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹא־ יֹ֤אמְרוּ עוֹד֙ חַי־ יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֶעֱלָ֛ה אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Instead they will say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives, who brought and led the descendants of the house of Israel up out of the land of the north and all the other lands to which He had banished them.’ Then they will dwell once more in their own land.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD lives.
The LORD brought the descendants of Israel out of the land of the north.
The LORD brought them out of all the other lands where He had banished them.
The LORD led them back.
The people of Israel will live in their own land again.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ חַי־ יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶעֱלָה֩ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵבִ֜יא אֶת־ זֶ֨רַע בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹנָה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָֽאֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִדַּחְתִּ֖ים שָׁ֑ם וְיָשְׁב֖וּ עַל־ אַדְמָתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: As for the prophets: My heart is broken within me, and all my bones tremble. I have become like a drunkard, like a man overcome by wine, because of the LORD, because of His holy words.
passages.sermon:
The prophets have caused me great distress.
My heart is broken inside me.
All my bones shake.
I feel like a man who is drunk.
I am like someone who has been overcome by wine.
The LORD is the reason for this.
His holy words have caused this in me.
passages.original: לַנְּבִאִ֞ים נִשְׁבַּ֧ר לִבִּ֣י בְקִרְבִּ֗י רָֽחֲפוּ֙ כָּל־ עַצְמוֹתַ֔י הָיִ֙יתִי֙ כְּאִ֣ישׁ שִׁכּ֔וֹר וּכְגֶ֖בֶר עֲבָ֣רוֹ יָ֑יִן מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וּמִפְּנֵ֖י דִּבְרֵ֥י קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: For the land is full of adulterers— because of the curse, the land mourns and the pastures of the wilderness have dried up— their course is evil and their power is misused.
passages.sermon:
The land is full of adulterers.
A curse covers the land.
The land mourns.
The pastures in the wilderness have dried up.
The people follow an evil path.
They misuse their power.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מְנָֽאֲפִים֙ מָלְאָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־ מִפְּנֵ֤י אָלָה֙ אָבְלָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ יָבְשׁ֖וּ נְא֣וֹת מִדְבָּ֑ר וַתְּהִ֤י מְרֽוּצָתָם֙ רָעָ֔ה וּגְבוּרָתָ֖ם לֹא־ כֵֽן׃

passages.text: “For both prophet and priest are ungodly; even in My house I have found their wickedness,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon: The LORD speaks.\r\nThe LORD says both the prophet and the priest are ungodly.\r\nThe LORD says He has found their wickedness even in His own house.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ גַם־ נָבִ֥יא גַם־ כֹּהֵ֖ן חָנֵ֑פוּ גַּם־ בְּבֵיתִ֛י מָצָ֥אתִי רָעָתָ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Therefore their path will become slick; they will be driven away into the darkness and fall into it. For I will bring disaster upon them in the year of their punishment,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the prophets and priests who are ungodly.
Their path will become slippery.
They will walk in darkness.
They will be pushed away.
They will fall in that darkness.
The LORD will bring disaster upon them.
This will happen in the year of their punishment.
The LORD has declared this.
passages.original: לָכֵן֩ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה דַרְכָּ֜ם לָהֶ֗ם כַּחֲלַקְלַקּוֹת֙ בָּֽאֲפֵלָ֔ה יִדַּ֖חוּ וְנָ֣פְלוּ בָ֑הּ כִּֽי־ אָבִ֨יא עֲלֵיהֶ֥ם רָעָ֛ה שְׁנַ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Among the prophets of Samaria I saw an offensive thing: They prophesied by Baal and led My people Israel astray.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the prophets of Samaria.
The prophets of Samaria did something offensive.
They prophesied by Baal.
They led the people of Israel astray.
The people of Israel are God's people.
The prophets of Samaria turned God's people away from Him.
passages.original: וּבִנְבִיאֵ֥י שֹׁמְר֖וֹן רָאִ֣יתִי תִפְלָ֑ה הִנַּבְּא֣וּ בַבַּ֔עַל וַיַּתְע֥וּ אֶת־ עַמִּ֖י אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: And among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: They commit adultery and walk in lies. They strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns his back on wickedness. They are all like Sodom to Me; the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the prophets of Jerusalem.
The LORD has seen a horrible thing among them.
These prophets commit adultery.
They walk in lies.
They make evildoers stronger.
No one turns away from wickedness because of them.
To the LORD, all these prophets are like the people of Sodom.
The people of Jerusalem are like the people of Gomorrah to the LORD.
passages.original: וּבִנְבִאֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם רָאִ֣יתִי שַׁעֲרוּרָ֗ה נָא֞וֹף וְהָלֹ֤ךְ בַּשֶּׁ֙קֶר֙ וְחִזְּקוּ֙ יְדֵ֣י מְרֵעִ֔ים לְבִ֨לְתִּי־ שָׁ֔בוּ אִ֖ישׁ מֵרָֽעָת֑וֹ הָֽיוּ־ לִ֤י כֻלָּם֙ כִּסְדֹ֔ם וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כַּעֲמֹרָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts says concerning the prophets: “I will feed them wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink, for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has spread throughout the land.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks about the prophets.
He says, “I will feed these prophets bitter food.
I will give them poisoned water to drink.
The prophets of Jerusalem have spread ungodliness.
Ungodliness has gone out from them to all the land.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ עַל־ הַנְּבִאִ֔ים הִנְנִ֨י מַאֲכִ֤יל אוֹתָם֙ לַֽעֲנָ֔ה וְהִשְׁקִתִ֖ים מֵי־ רֹ֑אשׁ כִּ֗י מֵאֵת֙ נְבִיאֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם יָצְאָ֥ה חֲנֻפָּ֖ה לְכָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃פ

passages.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They are filling you with false hopes. They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He gives a command.
Do not listen to the prophets who prophesy to you.
These prophets fill you with false hopes.
They speak visions from their own minds.
They do not speak from the mouth of the LORD.
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אַֽל־ תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ עַל־ דִּבְרֵ֤י הַנְּבִאִים֙ הַנִּבְּאִ֣ים לָכֶ֔ם מַהְבִּלִ֥ים הֵ֖מָּה אֶתְכֶ֑ם חֲז֤וֹן לִבָּם֙ יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ לֹ֖א מִפִּ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: They keep saying to those who despise Me, ‘The LORD says that you will have peace,’ and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart, ‘No harm will come to you.’
passages.sermon:
False prophets speak to people who reject God.
They say to these people, “The LORD says you will have peace.”
They also speak to everyone who follows his own stubborn heart.
They say, “No harm will come to you.”
passages.original: אֹמְרִ֤ים אָמוֹר֙ לִֽמְנַאֲצַ֔י דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׁל֖וֹם יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם וְ֠כֹל הֹלֵ֞ךְ בִּשְׁרִר֤וּת לִבּוֹ֙ אָֽמְר֔וּ לֹֽא־ תָב֥וֹא עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: But which of them has stood in the council of the LORD to see and hear His word? Who has given heed to His word and obeyed it?
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is speaking.
He asks about the false prophets.
He says, "Who among them has stood in My council?"
He asks, "Who has seen My word?"
He asks, "Who has heard My word?"
He asks, "Who has listened to My word and obeyed it?"
passages.original: כִּ֣י מִ֤י עָמַד֙ בְּס֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה וְיֵ֖רֶא וְיִשְׁמַ֣ע אֶת־ דְּבָר֑וֹ מִֽי־ הִקְשִׁ֥יב דְּבָרִי וַיִּשְׁמָֽע׃ס

passages.text: Behold, the storm of the LORD has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down upon the heads of the wicked.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is angry.
The LORD sends out a storm.
The storm is fierce.
A whirlwind spins with power.
The whirlwind falls on the wicked.
The storm strikes the heads of evil people.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה׀ סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה וְסַ֖עַר מִתְחוֹלֵ֑ל עַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ רְשָׁעִ֖ים יָחֽוּל׃

passages.text: The anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart. In the days to come you will understand this clearly.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has anger.
The LORD will not turn back His anger.
He will keep His anger until He finishes what He plans.
He will do everything He wants in His heart.
In the last days, you will understand this.
You will see it clearly.
passages.original: לֹ֤א יָשׁוּב֙ אַף־ יְהוָ֔ה עַד־ עֲשֹׂת֥וֹ וְעַד־ הֲקִימ֖וֹ מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ בְּאַֽחֲרִית֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים תִּתְבּ֥וֹנְנוּ בָ֖הּ בִּינָֽה׃

passages.text: I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message; I did not speak to them, yet they have prophesied.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about false prophets.
The LORD did not send these prophets.
These prophets ran with their own message.
The LORD did not speak to them.
These prophets still prophesied.
passages.original: לֹא־ שָׁלַ֥חְתִּי אֶת־ הַנְּבִאִ֖ים וְהֵ֣ם רָ֑צוּ לֹא־ דִבַּ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וְהֵ֥ם נִבָּֽאוּ׃

passages.text: But if they had stood in My council, they would have proclaimed My words to My people and turned them back from their evil ways and deeds.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks these words.
God is wise and holy.
God has a council.
The false prophets did not stand in God's council.
If the prophets had stood in God's council, they would have heard God's words.
If they had heard God's words, they would have spoken God's words to the people.
If the prophets had spoken God's words, the people would have turned from their evil ways.
The people would have turned from their evil deeds.
passages.original: וְאִֽם־ עָמְד֖וּ בְּסוֹדִ֑י וְיַשְׁמִ֤עוּ דְבָרַי֙ אֶת־ עַמִּ֔י וִֽישִׁבוּם֙ מִדַּרְכָּ֣ם הָרָ֔ע וּמֵרֹ֖עַ מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: “Am I only a God nearby,” declares the LORD, “and not a God far away?”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is God.
The LORD asks a question.
The LORD says, “Am I only a God who is near?”
The LORD says, “Am I not also a God who is far away?”
passages.original: הַאֱלֹהֵ֧י מִקָּרֹ֛ב אָ֖נִי נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א אֱלֹהֵ֖י מֵרָחֹֽק׃

passages.text: “Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” declares the LORD. “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD sees everything.
No one can hide from the LORD.
No man can hide in any secret place where the LORD cannot see him.
The LORD fills the heavens.
The LORD fills the earth.
The LORD declares these things.
passages.original: אִם־ יִסָּתֵ֨ר אִ֧ישׁ בַּמִּסְתָּרִ֛ים וַאֲנִ֥י לֹֽא־ אֶרְאֶ֖נּוּ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה הֲל֨וֹא אֶת־ הַשָּׁמַ֧יִם וְאֶת־ הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲנִ֥י מָלֵ֖א נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “I have heard the sayings of the prophets who prophesy lies in My name: ‘I had a dream! I had a dream!’
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD hears everything.
Some people call themselves prophets.
These prophets claim to speak in the name of the LORD.
These prophets do not tell the truth.
They speak lies.
They say, “I had a dream! I had a dream!”
They use these dreams to claim authority.
The LORD knows what they say.
passages.original: שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־ אָֽמְרוּ֙ הַנְּבִאִ֔ים הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים בִּשְׁמִ֛י שֶׁ֖קֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר חָלַ֖מְתִּי חָלָֽמְתִּי׃

passages.text: How long will this continue in the hearts of these prophets who prophesy falsehood, these prophets of the delusion of their own minds?
passages.sermon:
God speaks about false prophets.
These prophets claim to speak for God.
They do not tell the truth.
They speak lies.
They follow their own minds.
They believe their own delusions.
God asks, “How long will this go on in their hearts?”
These prophets keep falsehood in their hearts.
They continue to deceive themselves and others.
passages.original: עַד־ מָתַ֗י הֲיֵ֛שׁ בְּלֵ֥ב הַנְּבִאִ֖ים נִבְּאֵ֣י הַשָּׁ֑קֶר וּנְבִיאֵ֖י תַּרְמִ֥ת לִבָּֽם׃

passages.text: They suppose the dreams that they tell one another will make My people forget My name, just as their fathers forgot My name through the worship of Baal.
passages.sermon:
Some prophets tell dreams to each other.
These prophets think their dreams will make My people forget My name.
Their fathers forgot My name before.
Their fathers forgot My name because they worshiped Baal.
passages.original: הַחֹשְׁבִ֗ים לְהַשְׁכִּ֤יחַ אֶת־ עַמִּי֙ שְׁמִ֔י בַּחֲל֣וֹמֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְסַפְּר֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁכְח֧וּ אֲבוֹתָ֛ם אֶת־ שְׁמִ֖י בַּבָּֽעַל׃

passages.text: Let the prophet who has a dream retell it, but let him who has My word speak it truthfully. For what is straw compared to grain?” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says, “Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream.
Let the one who has My word speak My word truthfully.
Straw and grain are not the same.
My word is like grain.
A dream is like straw.
There is a great difference between them.
This is what the LORD declares.”
passages.original: הַנָּבִ֞יא אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֤וֹ חֲלוֹם֙ יְסַפֵּ֣ר חֲל֔וֹם וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר דְּבָרִי֙ אִתּ֔וֹ יְדַבֵּ֥ר דְּבָרִ֖י אֱמֶ֑ת מַה־ לַתֶּ֥בֶן אֶת־ הַבָּ֖ר נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Is not My word like fire,” declares the LORD, “and like a hammer that smashes a rock?”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD has great power and authority.
The LORD says, “My word is like fire.”
Fire burns and consumes.
The LORD says, “My word is like a hammer.”
A hammer breaks a rock into pieces.
My word is strong.
My word changes what it touches.
passages.original: הֲל֨וֹא כֹ֧ה דְבָרִ֛י כָּאֵ֖שׁ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וּכְפַטִּ֖ישׁ יְפֹ֥צֵֽץ סָֽלַע׃ס

passages.text: “Therefore behold,” declares the LORD, “I am against the prophets who steal from one another words they attribute to Me.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says, “I am against the prophets.”
These prophets steal words from each other.
They claim these words come from Me.
I, the LORD, oppose them.
passages.original: לָכֵ֛ן הִנְנִ֥י עַל־ הַנְּבִאִ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה מְגַנְּבֵ֣י דְבָרַ֔י אִ֖ישׁ מֵאֵ֥ת רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: “Yes,” declares the LORD, “I am against the prophets who wag their own tongues and proclaim, ‘The LORD declares it.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says, “I am against the prophets.”
These prophets use their own tongues to speak.
They claim, ‘The LORD declares it.’
They do not speak My true words.
They use their own words and pretend they come from Me.
I, the LORD, oppose these prophets.
passages.original: הִנְנִ֥י עַל־ הַנְּבִיאִ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה הַלֹּקְחִ֣ים לְשׁוֹנָ֔ם וַֽיִּנְאֲמ֖וּ נְאֻֽם׃

passages.text: “Indeed,” declares the LORD, “I am against those who prophesy false dreams and retell them to lead My people astray with their reckless lies. It was not I who sent them or commanded them, and they are of no benefit at all to these people,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is against certain prophets.
These prophets claim to have dreams.
Their dreams are false.
These prophets tell their false dreams to others.
They lead God's people astray.
They use lies and act recklessly.
The LORD did not send these prophets.
The LORD did not command them.
These prophets do not help the people at all.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: הִ֠נְנִי עַֽל־ נִבְּאֵ֞י חֲלֹמ֥וֹת שֶׁ֙קֶר֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיְסַפְּרוּם֙ וַיַּתְע֣וּ אֶת־ עַמִּ֔י בְּשִׁקְרֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְפַחֲזוּתָ֑ם וְאָנֹכִ֨י לֹֽא־ שְׁלַחְתִּ֜ים וְלֹ֣א צִוִּיתִ֗ים וְהוֹעֵ֛יל לֹֽא־ יוֹעִ֥ילוּ לָֽעָם־ הַזֶּ֖ה נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Now when this people or a prophet or priest asks you, ‘What is the burden of the LORD?’ you are to say to them, ‘What burden? I will forsake you, declares the LORD.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Jeremiah.
The LORD gives Jeremiah a message for the people, prophets, and priests.
The people, prophets, or priests may ask Jeremiah a question.
They may ask, "What is the burden of the LORD?"
Jeremiah must answer them.
He must say, "What burden?"
The LORD declares, "I will forsake you."
The LORD gives this message as a warning.
passages.original: וְכִי־ יִשְׁאָלְךָ֩ הָעָ֨ם הַזֶּ֜ה אֽוֹ־ הַנָּבִ֤יא אֽוֹ־ כֹהֵן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַה־ מַשָּׂ֖א יְהוָ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־ מַה־ מַשָּׂ֔א וְנָטַשְׁתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: As for the prophet or priest or anyone who claims, ‘This is the burden of the LORD,’ I will punish that man and his household.
passages.sermon:
God speaks with authority.
God is the LORD.
A prophet may claim, “This is the burden of the LORD.”
A priest may claim, “This is the burden of the LORD.”
Any person may claim, “This is the burden of the LORD.”
God will act against that person.
God will punish that person.
God will also punish that person’s household.
passages.original: וְהַנָּבִ֤יא וְהַכֹּהֵן֙ וְהָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹאמַ֖ר מַשָּׂ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּפָקַדְתִּ֛י עַל־ הָאִ֥ישׁ הַה֖וּא וְעַל־ בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: This is what each man is to say to his friend and to his brother: ‘What has the LORD answered?’ or ‘What has the LORD spoken?’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel through Jeremiah.
God gave instructions to the people.
God told each person what to say to others.
Each man must speak to his friend.
Each man must speak to his brother.
He must ask, “What has the LORD answered?”
He must also ask, “What has the LORD spoken?”
passages.original: כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֛וּ אִ֥ישׁ עַל־ רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְאִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ אָחִ֑יו מֶה־ עָנָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה וּמַה־ דִּבֶּ֖ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: But refer no more to the burden of the LORD, for each man’s word becomes the burden, so that you pervert the words of the living God, the LORD of Hosts, our God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the living God.
He is our God.
Do not say, "The burden of the LORD" anymore.
Each man makes his own word into a burden.
You change and twist the words of the living God.
passages.original: וּמַשָּׂ֥א יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א תִזְכְּרוּ־ ע֑וֹד כִּ֣י הַמַּשָּׂ֗א יִֽהְיֶה֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ דְּבָר֔וֹ וַהֲפַכְתֶּ֗ם אֶת־ דִּבְרֵי֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַיִּ֔ים יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Thus you are to say to the prophet: ‘What has the LORD answered you?’ and ‘What has the LORD spoken?’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jeremiah the prophet.
God told Jeremiah what to say to the people.
God said, “Speak to the prophet.”
Ask the prophet, ‘What has the LORD answered you?’
Ask the prophet, ‘What has the LORD spoken?’
passages.original: כֹּ֥ה תֹאמַ֖ר אֶל־ הַנָּבִ֑יא מֶה־ עָנָ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה וּמַה־ דִּבֶּ֖ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: But if you claim, ‘This is the burden of the LORD,’ then this is what the LORD says: Because you have said, ‘This is the burden of the LORD,’ and I specifically told you not to make this claim, therefore I will surely forget you and will cast you out of My presence, both you and the city that I gave to you and your fathers.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the living God.
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
The LORD gave a command to His people.
He told them not to say, "This is the burden of the LORD."
If you say, "This is the burden of the LORD," you disobey His command.
The LORD says this to you.
Because you have said, "This is the burden of the LORD," after I told you not to say it, I will act against you.
I will forget you.
I will lift you up and carry you away.
I will abandon you.
I will abandon the city I gave to you and to your fathers.
I will remove you and your city from My presence.
passages.original: וְאִם־ מַשָּׂ֣א יְהוָה֮ תֹּאמֵרוּ֒ לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה יַ֧עַן אֲמָרְכֶ֛ם אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה מַשָּׂ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וָאֶשְׁלַ֤ח אֲלֵיכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאמְר֖וּ מַשָּׂ֥א יְהוָֽה׃ לָכֵ֣ן הִנְנִ֔י וְנָשִׁ֥יתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם נָשֹׁ֑א וְנָטַשְׁתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֗ם וְאֶת־ הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧תִּי לָכֶ֛ם וְלַאֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם מֵעַ֥ל פָּנָֽי׃

passages.text: And I will bring upon you everlasting shame and perpetual humiliation that will never be forgotten.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to the people of Judah.
The LORD said He will bring shame upon them.
This shame will last forever.
The LORD said He will bring humiliation upon them.
This humiliation will never end.
No one will ever forget this shame and humiliation.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֥י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם חֶרְפַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם וּכְלִמּ֣וּת עוֹלָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א תִשָּׁכֵֽחַ׃ס
